# How many curtain panels do I need?

> Convert curtain pole or track width, heading fullness ratio, and single-panel flat width into a whole-panel order count—and inspect the actual fullness after rounding.

## Calculator
- [Open the calculator](https://calculationgrove.com/): US window: a 72 in rod at 2× fullness needs 144 in flat width; with 50 in panels in even pairs, order 4 panels (200 in flat width, 2.78× fullness). Metric: a 180 cm track at 2× fullness needs 360 cm flat width; buying even pairs of 140 cm panels requires 4 panels (3.11× actual fullness).

## Guide
- [How to work out how many curtain panels you need](https://calculationgrove.com/guide/): step-by-step measuring, common mistakes, and ordering checklist.

## Formula and method
Target flat width = track width × desired fullness; Panels = ceiling(target flat width / panel width) (rounded up to next even number for center-opening pairs); Actual fullness = (panels × panel width) / track width.

Multiply the full curtain rod or track width by your desired fullness multiplier to get the target combined flat width. Divide by the flat finished width of one panel and round up. When buying symmetrical pairs, increment any odd result by one panel, then recompute actual fullness.

## Limits
Measure the full rod between finials or full track length, not just window glass. Blackout wraparound returns, center overlap, extra-thick thermal linings, and finished drop length are separate measurements.

## Curtain heading styles, typical fullness, and standard panel widths

Ready-made US panels commonly measure 50 to 54 in flat width; UK ready-made widths are typically 46, 66, or 90 in per panel.

| Heading style | Recommended fullness | Look when closed | Common retail panel width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eyelet / grommet | 1.5× – 2.0× | Deep, crisp modern waves | 50–54 in (132–140 cm) |
| Tab top / back tab | 1.5× – 2.0× | Relaxed casual pleats | 50–52 in (127–135 cm) |
| Wave / ripplefold | 1.8× – 2.2× | Uniform architectural S-folds | Custom or 54 in+ |
| Rod pocket | 2.0× – 2.5× | Soft gathered folds | 50–54 in (127–140 cm) |
| Pencil / pinch pleat | 2.0× – 2.5× | Tailored formal drapery | 46, 66, or 90 in (UK) / 50 in+ (US) |
| Sheer panels | 2.5× – 3.0× | Airy layered privacy | 52–59 in (132–150 cm) |

## Step by step
1. Measure the total width of the curtain pole (between finials) or track—not the window glass alone. Standard rods extend 6 to 12 in (15 to 30 cm) past each side of the frame.
2. Pick a fullness multiplier for your heading style: 1.5× to 2× for tailored grommet or eyelet headings, and 2× to 2.5× for rod-pocket, pencil-pleat, or pinch-pleat drapes.
3. Read the flat width of a single finished panel on the package (common US ready-made panels are 50 or 52 in wide; UK panels are often 46, 66, or 90 in).
4. Keep the even-pairs option checked for center-opening windows so both sides hang symmetrically.

## Common mistakes
- Measuring only the glass width, which leaves light leaks and blocks daylight when curtains are pulled open.
- Assuming "1× fullness" covers a window neatly. Flat panels stretch tight like a sheet and rarely meet cleanly in the center.
- Forgetting return and overlap width on wraparound blackout rods or heavy lined drapes.
- Mixing up pair width with single-panel width when reading online retail product listings.

## Worked examples
### Example 1
Metric: a 180 cm track at 2× fullness needs 360 cm flat width; buying even pairs of 140 cm panels requires 4 panels (3.11× actual fullness).

### Example 2
US window: a 72 in rod at 2× fullness needs 144 in flat width; with 50 in panels in even pairs, order 4 panels (200 in flat width, 2.78× fullness).
